question: What is the primary goal of a school health programme?

options.A: Train students to become professional nurses
options.B: Provide full medical treatment for community members
options.C: Focus strictly on academic performance enhancement
options.D: Promote optimal health and well-being of learners

explanation: The primary objective revolves around protecting and improving the health status of students to enhance learning. [learn more](GNS225_U4_T2#GNS225_U4_T2_h1)

question: Why must a school health programme involve the local community?

options.A: To ensure compliance with strict national building codes
options.B: To sustain student wellness through shared resources
options.C: To reduce the financial burden on the teaching staff
options.D: To replace the need for professional school nurses

explanation: Community integration bridges home and school environments, making health interventions more sustainable. [learn more](GNS225_U4_T2#GNS225_U4_T2_h1)

question: A physical component of a healthful school environment is...

options.B: Reliable sources of safe drinking water

explanation: Safe water is a fundamental physical infrastructure requirement to prevent waterborne illnesses in schools. [learn more](GNS225_U4_T2#GNS225_U4_T2_h2)

question: What is a major public health hazard found in many under-resourced schools?

options.C: Excessive use of modern technology devices
options.D: Lack of clean water and proper latrines

explanation: Inadequate sanitation infrastructure directly contributes to the spread of communicable diseases among students. [learn more](GNS225_U4_T2#GNS225_U4_T2_h2)

question: Who typically takes the lead role in delivering school health services on-site?
explanation: Nurses are uniquely trained to conduct screenings, administer first aid, and coordinate health referrals in schools. [learn more](GNS225_U4_T2#GNS225_U4_T2_h3)

question: A student sustains a deep laceration while playing football on the school field. What is the immediate nursing action?

options.A: Administer first aid and evaluate for referral
options.B: Wait until closing hours to notify the parents
options.C: Encourage the student to wash it with playground soil
options.D: Refer the child straight to a tertiary hospital

explanation: Immediate first aid stabilizes the injury, after which the nurse determines if advanced medical care is necessary. [learn more](GNS225_U4_T2#GNS225_U4_T2_h3)

question: The primary purpose of health education in schools is to...

options.B: Replace the biological sciences curriculum entirely
options.C: Empower students to adopt healthy lifestyle habits
options.D: Generate revenue for school health clinics

explanation: Health education aims to bridge the gap between knowing health facts and practicing healthy behaviors. [learn more](GNS225_U4_T2#GNS225_U4_T2_h4)

question: Which teaching approach is most effective when delivering health education to adolescents?

options.A: Strict memorization of medical textbook chapters

explanation: Interactive methods engage young learners and encourage them to critically evaluate their own health behaviors. [learn more](GNS225_U4_T2#GNS225_U4_T2_h4)

question: A major benefit of school feeding programmes for young learners is...

options.A: Improved cognitive function and learning capacity
options.B: Complete elimination of all hereditary diseases
options.C: Reduction in the number of school holidays

explanation: Proper nutrition fuels the brain, directly improving concentration, attendance, and academic performance. [learn more](GNS225_U4_T2#GNS225_U4_T2_h5)

question: What is an important responsibility of a nurse regarding school food vendors?

options.A: Cooking the meals personally before service
options.B: Determining the daily market prices of food items
options.C: Monitoring basic food safety and hygiene practices
options.D: Selecting which farmers receive government contracts

explanation: Nurses safeguard student health by ensuring that food handlers maintain high hygiene standards to prevent foodborne illness. [learn more](GNS225_U4_T2#GNS225_U4_T2_h5)

question: Which of the following is a common psychosocial stressor for school-age children?
explanation: Children and adolescents frequently experience intense stress related to school performance and social acceptance. [learn more](GNS225_U4_T2#GNS225_U4_T2_h6)

question: When a student exhibits sudden withdrawal and declining academic performance, the nurse should suspect...

options.A: That the student is intentionally avoiding sports
options.B: Underlying emotional distress or mental health challenges
options.C: That the student requires immediate dental surgery
options.D: A temporary lack of interest in extracurriculars

explanation: Behavioral shifts and academic drops are classic red flags signaling potential mental health struggles. [learn more](GNS225_U4_T2#GNS225_U4_T2_h6)

question: What is the primary purpose of evaluation in a school health programme?

options.A: Increase tuition fees for health maintenance
options.B: Reduce the total number of enrolled students
options.C: Identify service gaps and measure goal achievement
options.D: Punish schools that fail to meet academic targets

explanation: Evaluation provides data to determine whether health interventions are working and where improvements are needed. [learn more](GNS225_U4_T2#GNS225_U4_T2_h7)

question: Which activity forms part of quality assurance for school health services?

options.A: Auditing student health records and tracking immunization coverage
options.B: Conducting random fitness tests for the teaching staff
options.C: Inspecting the personal bank accounts of school administrators
options.D: Evaluating the teaching qualifications of mathematics instructors

explanation: Reviewing medical logs and vaccine tallies ensures accountability and consistent delivery of clinical care. [learn more](GNS225_U4_T2#GNS225_U4_T2_h7)
